camera.baseline: Patient side, eye level, horizontal frame.
camera.independent_optional_refinement: Place the camera diagonally along the public counter at a modest three-quarter view of the woman. Keep her face nearest the lens, hands below it, clear staff-side record window beside her, and the exit immediately behind rather than at the remote corridor end.
camera.why: A lateral barrier view can show the woman's visible face and the chart beyond the glass without forcing the camera onto the staff side.
camera.ownership: Agent-owned; camera remains open. No new requester-axis requirement.

glass_boundary.state: Closed hatch at the shutter; clear lower glass separates the chart from the woman.
endpoint_trace: Woman and both hands stay on the public side.
Sleeve opening rests on the public counter.
Right fingertips rest on the projecting public-side hatch lip.
Staff-side chart has no contact route to either hand.
glass_boundary.risk: Reflection or a counter edge alone may be mistaken for the closed barrier. The hatch and glazing boundary must have visible framing.

hands.left: Holds only the light empty sleeve; fingers pinch its open top while its lower edge can rest on the counter.
hands.right: Fingertips rest on the adjacent hatch ledge, with the wrist and forearm visibly reaching from the same torso.
hands.simultaneous_feasibility: Both forearms reach forward a short distance to neighboring regions at waist level. Neither hand operates the door bolt. No hand passes through glass or carries the retained chart.
hands.risk: Loose plastic may visually merge with the closed hatch or be filled with papers by the generator. Treat indistinct sleeve emptiness as partial/fail.

chart.state: A separate retained record exists beyond the glass.
chart.independent_optional_refinement: Stand or lean the staff-side chart so its outer folder and clipped portrait face the public window. This is a prospective visibility refinement within open prop placement and composition.
chart.risk: A flat chart photographed from eye level may conceal its face or appear to be on the woman's counter. The small duplicate portrait is authorial, not a hard identity proof.

exit.state: Door is closed; a real bolt crosses the door seam.
exit.independent_optional_refinement: Keep the doorway adjacent to the counter in the near background and give the bolt enough edge contrast to separate it from a generic door handle.
exit.risk: A red lamp, handle, rectangular panel, or bar that does not span the seam cannot establish the intended locked state. Perspective must leave both bolt endpoints legible.

priority_order: Closed boundary and distinct retained chart
projection.depth_strategy: Compact counter-to-door space; do not put the diagnostic bolt at the vanishing point. Keep enough depth of field for the handover boundary and door mechanism rather than turning all context into blur.
projection.scale_boundary: Full original saved image is mandatory for assessment. A blurred or tiny component remains unobservable after enlargement.

anticipated_claim_limits: Exact record ownership cannot be established from an unresolved clipped portrait; report that limit.
A bolt proves an obstructed door only when its endpoints and seam are visible; it does not prove the institution's unseen motive.
A face expression alone cannot prove coercion, diagnosis, consent, or real inner life.
Institutional dread is a qualitative whole-scene observation distinct from physical relation gates.
No preflight text is a rendered-pixel PASS.
